summary: A one-day first week: the desk opened Friday into an AI-led rout (S&P -2.7% and Nasdaq -5% for the week, VIX 25.6 after 28 on Friday, oil -13%, gold +4.5%). Sam's earnings gap-and-hold buys carried the desk (+C$38.47); Fox's gold breakout faded (-C$82.50); Dax and Vega made no trades; Lena's six trades were the stop-sign bug, fixed Friday evening. The C$200 bonus for this week was forfeited by the owner: no payout, nothing carried over.

day: No trades: on a gap-down rout no 15-minute opening-range break came with the volume his rules need. The filter did its job.
His meeting plan was right to wait (two losses and done), but a whole day without a setup means his scan list was too narrow for a high-VIX open.
Next week: more attempts allowed and a nearer target, so wins are banked before the fast reversals a VIX-25 tape brings.
swing: [Earnings gap-and-hold] made the desk's week: four buys (ABNB from the meeting, MGNI, U, XERS); XERS (+8%, beat by 125%) carried it while the other three sit about 1% under entry.
He is fully invested (C$19 cash), so a new setup Monday needs a sale first; the rate-rotation and breakout plays weren't used.
One order was cut to zero by the risk-off mood sizing: small positions round to nothing when the mood multiplier is 0.6.
long: Her six trades this week were the stop-sign bug (a stop above the buy price sold each buy within minutes), fixed Friday evening; the +C$2.18 is noise, not a verdict on [Dividend grower].
She starts next week all cash (C$3,001) with a correct 18% stop below every buy, no Monday tranche top-ups, and her own list plus the meeting's names.
LLY, the meeting's long-term pick, never filled: she can rebuild from her own list first.
futures: The meeting's gold breakout (buy above 4,090) filled, then gold slipped back to about 4,075: -C$82.50 open, stop near 4,010.
The breakout fired on a touch, not a close, in a risk-off tape where round-number breaks faded all day.
His second order was sized to zero by the mood multiplier (one contract x 0.8 rounds to nothing).
options_aggr: No trades: the meeting's one NVDA call was sized to zero because one contract x the 0.7 risk-off multiplier rounds down to nothing.
Waiting on the chip bounce was reasonable with Nov 17 earnings ahead, but a one-contract plan can never pass a mood cut.
Next week: slightly longer-dated options so a VIX-25 market's daily swings don't decide the trade.
options_safe: No cash-secured put qualified (with C$3,000 the stock must be under about US$20 and above its 200-day), so 82% of his cash sits in CASH.TO: the safe default working.
Premiums were rich (VIX 25-28), which is when a careful seller wants to be active.
Next week: strikes one step closer for more premium while staying the desk's safe player (aggression 4).
crypto: [Extreme-fear buy] fired twice in about seven hours (Fear & Greed 25), adding BTC and ETH; the core and growth buckets were already built, leaving 14% cash.
BTC and ETH are flat from his entries; XRP is down 3%, LINK and SOL up about 1%: -C$12.81 for the week.
His growth-coin stops sit about 30% below entry, which suits coins that swing 5-10% a day.

day: On a gap-down rout day (S&P futures -2%+, VIX 25+) clean 15-minute range breaks with volume are rare: zero trades is the filter working, not a failure.
swing: Earnings gap-and-hold names with a huge beat held best on a down day; small beats drifted with the market, so size the biggest beats first.
When fully invested, a new setup needs a planned sale: name which holding goes first.
long: A long-term buy needs its stop well below the price (about 18%); check every stop is under the buy before trusting a fill.
futures: Breakouts above a round number fade in a risk-off tape: buy on a 5-minute close above the level, not a touch.
options_aggr: One contract times a risk-off mood cut (0.7) rounds to zero: plan two contracts on a cheaper strike, or expect no fill on a risk-off day.
options_safe: With C$3,000 a cash-secured put needs a stock under about US$20 above its 200-day: table cheap quality names, or the cash stays parked.
crypto: One extreme-fear add per fear episode keeps cash for a deeper flush; two adds in a day left only 14% cash.

day.why: Zero trades on a rout day: one more attempt allowed and a nearer target to bank wins before VIX-25 reversals.

swing.why: Gap-and-hold names need a few more days to drift, and a VIX-25 market needs a little more room before a stop.

long.why: The stop bug, not her picks, emptied her book: one more position slot to rebuild from all cash.

futures.why: Breakouts are fading in this tape: take profit sooner.

options_aggr.why: Slightly longer-dated options so daily VIX-25 swings don't decide the trade.

options_safe.why: Rich premiums: strikes one step closer for more premium, still the safe player (4 is his ceiling).

crypto.why: Crypto swings widened with the equity sell-off: a little more room before stops on news and meme coins.
